text:
jess (Acme): Hi, hitting a production issue: when our app calls the invoice-generation tool via streaming, the tool args arrive as truncated JSON and the tool fails with schema error. Happens ~10% of invocations.

sarah (support): Sorry you're seeing that — can you paste the exact payload you send and the request id for a failing run? any proxy in front of your service?

jess (Acme): request_id=rid_20240317_42. We're on Node SDK v0.12.3, behind our edge nginx proxy. Here's the client payload we send (trimmed):
```json
{"tool":"generate_invoice","args":{"order_id":"ORD-998","items":[{"sku":"X12","qty":1}],"customer":{"id":"C-12"}
```
(this is what the server logs show for that request)

alert-bot: New error logged: runtime-toolcall-schema-fail rid=rid_20240317_42 status=400

sarah (support): thanks — tagging runtime eng. @dmitri can you take a look?

dmitri (eng-runtime): on it. quick question: does the failure happen only when using streaming API (SSE/keep-alive) vs non-streaming?

jess (Acme): yes, non-streaming POSTs to the same tool work fine. It's specifically streaming toolcall flow.

dmitri (eng-runtime): OK that's helpful. suspecting chunk-boundary split of the JSON args across SSE chunks; our streaming layer expects tool args to be emitted atomically but some proxies/chunkers can slice mid-object. can you confirm your nginx config (proxy_buffering, gzip, keepalive settings)?

jess (Acme): nginx config mostly default, we're using http1.1 keepalives and proxy_buffering on.

mike (oncall): reproducer attempt notes below. I ran a local repro that simulates a proxy slicing chunks:
```bash
# simulate the model stream emitting JSON args midstream then later finishing
echo -n '{"tool":"generate_invoice","args":{"order_id":"ORD-TEST","items":[{"sku":"X' > part1.txt
echo -n '12","qty":1}],"customer":{"id":"C-TEST"}}' > part2.txt
# send part1 then part2 with a tiny pause to simulate chunking
cat part1.txt | nc -l 9001 & sleep 0.05; cat part2.txt | nc localhost 9001
```
Result: consumer sees two separate chunks; our parser tried to validate the first chunk as full JSON -> schema error.

mike (oncall): reproduced on 0.12.3. Logs: `schema validation failed: unexpected end of JSON input at line 1` with rid matching.

dmitri (eng-runtime): confirmed reproduction. Root cause: the runtime emits toolcall args as streaming tokens; the service layer relied on TCP message boundaries being preserved. edge proxies (nginx with buffering on) sometimes flush partial buffers to client, producing mid-object splits.

sarah (support): what's the mitigation? customer needs something low-effort they can apply now.

dmitri (eng-runtime): two options: customer side and runtime side. Customer quick mitigation: set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection "";` and increase `proxy_read_timeout` on the nginx front to avoid premature flushes. That reduces chunk fragmentation.

jess (Acme): we can try that, but we'd prefer a server-side fix we don't have to touch infra for.

dmitri (eng-runtime): longer-term fix (we'll do): make the streaming parser resilient — buffer partial events until a complete JSON object is validated or until a framing boundary. Pragmatic approach: require toolcall args to be framed per SSE event (we already send `data:` frames) and treat each SSE event as an atomic payload, assembling multiple `data:` lines until a terminating blank line. We'll also add a small safety buffer to only attempt schema validation once we've parsed a complete JSON value.

mike (oncall): created internal ticket INF-7421 and drafted a hotfix branch: runtime: sse-toolcall-buffering. Plan: bump canary to 10% tomorrow, monitor rid errors and schema-fail rate.

dmitri (eng-runtime): short-term server-side hotfix we can push: if the JSON parser sees incomplete input it should not raise schema-fail; instead mark the request as streaming-incomplete and wait for more input (up to 2s or 2MB). That avoids false negatives. Implemented basic change and smoke-tested against the chunked repro — parser now waits for full object.

mike (oncall): deployed canary at 2024-03-18T04:30Z. Observed rid_... errors drop to 0 for test traffic.

sarah (support): jess — recommended path: apply nginx `proxy_buffering off` as a stopgap and we'll roll the runtime canary; we'll notify when the fix reaches hosted. Also offering a usage credit for affected calls.

jess (Acme): applied proxy_buffering off and saw immediate improvement in dev environment. Thanks. Please let us know the canary status and ETA for full deploy.

dmitri (eng-runtime): canary looks good. ETA for full rollout: 48 hours pending additional SLO checks. I'll post the PR and changelog.

sarah (support): filing a support ticket to track credits and closure. severity=high, customer impacted production feature.

mike (oncall): additional notes for postmortem: add test in runtime test-suite to simulate chunked SSE where JSON object spans multiple chunks; add Nginx config doc to troubleshooting KB.

sarah (support): closing loop: jess — we'll follow up when fully deployed and confirm credits. thanks for quick repro steps. :heart:

jess (Acme): appreciate it, thanks everyone :clap:
